articles.title: Pakistan equal India's historic Lord's chase record, clinch ODI tri-nation series - India Today
articles.summary: Pakistan equal India's historic Lord's chase record, clinch ODI tri-nation series India Today
articles.content: Pakistan produced a remarkable run chase to defeat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the final of the ODI tri-nation series in Lahore on Saturday, October 31. Chasing a daunting 326 at the Gaddafi Stadium, Pakistan rode on a magnificent century from Fakhar Zaman and crucial contributions from Saad Baig and Arafat Minhas to seal the title with nine balls to spare.The victory also saw Pakistan equal India's historic record for the highest successful run chase in an ODI tournament final. India had set the benchmark in 2002 when they chased down England's target of 326 in the NatWest Series final at Lord's.Yuvraj Singh and Mohammed Kaif had scripted one of the most memorable comebacks in Indian cricket, rescuing the team from a precarious position to secure a two-wicket win. Pakistan's achievement, 24 years later, put them alongside India in the record books.The triumph was particularly significant for Pakistan, who had not won an ODI tri-series title since the 2008 Kitply Cup in Bangladesh. Their latest success came after a high-pressure chase in which they recovered from an early collapse and held their nerve in the closing overs.HIGHEST SUCCESSFUL RUN-CHASE IN ODI FINALSIndia against England – 326 (2002, Lord's)Pakistan against Sri Lanka – 326 (2026, Lahore)India against Pakistan – 315 (1998, Dhaka)West Indies against Pakistan – 285 (1993, Sharjah)New Zealand against India – 277 (2005, Harare)KAMINDU, RATHNAYAKE POWER SRI LANKAAfter being asked to bat, Sri Lanka posted an imposing 325 for eight in their 50 overs, with Kamindu Mendis leading the charge with his maiden ODI century. The left-hander struck a superb 131 off 128 balls, hitting 12 fours and two sixes to give his side a strong platform.Kamindu found early support from Avishka Fernando, who scored 38 as the pair added 87 runs for the opening wicket. However, it was his partnership with Pavan Rathnayake that truly put Sri Lanka in a commanding position. The duo added 146 runs for the third wicket, with Rathnayake contributing an attacking 77 off 65 deliveries.Pakistan needed breakthroughs to prevent Sri Lanka from running away with the contest, and captain Shaheen Shah Afridi provided them at crucial moments. He dismissed Kamindu and Dasun Shanaka in quick succession, while Haris Rauf and Naseem Shah also picked up two wickets apiece. Pakistan's bowlers fought back in the closing stages, taking six wickets in the final 10 overs to restrict Sri Lanka to 325.FAKHAR, MINHAS LEAD PAKISTAN HOMEPakistan's chase suffered an early setback as Maaz Sadaqat fell for five before Babar Azam was dismissed for a duck. At 14 for two, the hosts were under considerable pressure, but Fakhar Zaman refused to let the situation dictate the tempo of the innings.Fakhar joined Saad Baig to rebuild the chase, and the pair added 149 runs for the third wicket. Baig played a composed knock of 74, while Fakhar took the attack to the Sri Lankan bowlers, bringing up a magnificent 127 off 99 balls. His innings included 11 fours and six sixes before Dilshan Madushanka finally dismissed him.Sri Lanka briefly sensed an opportunity when Fakhar and Salman Ali Agha departed, leaving Pakistan needing a substantial contribution from their lower order. Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz then produced the decisive partnership, adding 94 runs to turn the contest back in Pakistan's favour. Minhas smashed 61 off just 31 balls, while Nawaz held his nerve at the other end.Minhas fell with victory within touching distance, and Faheem Ashraf was dismissed for a golden duck. With two runs needed, Shaheen finished the contest in emphatic fashion, launching Madushanka over the boundary for a six.- Ends

articles.title: Youth Olympic Games: The curious case of India’s approach | Hindustan Times - Hindustan Times
articles.summary: Youth Olympic Games: The curious case of India’s approach | Hindustan Times Hindustan Times
articles.content: Did you know there’s a pretty important Olympics starting this weekend? And that India’s got athletes in it? Read or saw anything about them? Who designed their ceremonial kit etc., etc.? No, no, no and no?Well, that’s how much enthusiasm the Indian sporting establishment appears to have around the 2026 Youth Olympic Games (YOG) being held in Africa for the first time, in the Senegalese capital of Dakar (October 31-November 13), across 25 competition (medal) sports with a Games motto of “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates.”In the Senegalese native Wolof, that’s “Afrig Dalal, Ndakaaru Jëmël” and “L’Afrique accueille, Dakar célèbre” in French. The YOG are a relatively new competition, first held in Singapore 2010 as the Summer YOG with Innsbruck 2012 marking the first winter youth Olympics. The age criteria for Dakar 2026 stipulates that no athlete can be younger than 14 and older than 17 at the time of competing.India is sending its smallest YOG contingent — 17 athletes with 11 girls and six boys across 11 disciplines — having won 23 medals across the previous three editions. India’s best YOG performance came in the previous edition — Buenos Aires 2018 — with 13 medals from a contingent of 46. Before casting an eye on India’s 17 for Dakar 2026, let’s look closer at the 2018 numbers.India won seven of its 13 YOG medals in 2018 across three sports which do not feature this time: hockey (five-a-side which adds to contingent numbers – 18 - but not Olympic-level continuity/relevance), shooting and weightlifting. Take away the hockey squad, plus four shooters and two wrestlers and that still leaves us with 22, five more than we have sent to Dakar2026.Do those extra athletes matter? Yes. Because if this clutch of Indian athletes — average age just over 16 — are expected to be ready, if not for LA2028 at least Brisbane 2032, then competing with the global cream of their age group marks both a reality check and provides the impetus to push ahead.Announcing the contingent, IOA President PT Usha said, “Dakar2026 is an important milestone for our young athletes. They represent the future of Indian sport and among them may be the champions who will represent India at Brisbane2032 and beyond.”If we look back at Buenos Aires 2018, India’s medallists were Manu Bhaker, Saurabh Chaudhary, Lakshya Sen and Jeremy Lalrinnunga in individual sport, and amongst the hockey players we had Salima Tete, Lalremsiami, Bichudevi Kharibam and Vivek Sagar Prasad, who was part of the Indian hockey team that won back-to-back bronze medals in the Tokyo and Paris Olympics.ALSO READ: PT Usha, Gagan Narang, Adille Sumariwalla in draft list of nominations for SOM electionAmongst other Indian performers, HS Prannoy, Yuki Bhambri, Shiva Thapa, Srihari Nataraj, Advait Page, Manav Thakkar and Archana Kamath have also been part of YOG contingents.Globally, there is a particulary revealing list on Olympedia.com of at least 311 athletes who graduated from being summer YOG medallists to summer Olympic Games (OG) medallists. Manu, Vivek plus hockey defender Sanjay Rana are on it, but so are Chad Le Clos, Noah Lyles, Salwa Eid Nasar and Ma Ning.There is some debate about the relevance of the YOG in terms of the calendar and training schedules of athletes across some sport. There are others where the YOG to OG transition is an accurate progress tracker. Definitely in swimming and athletics (not Indian strongholds) but also boxing, judo and table tennis where India has some skin in the game.In Dakar 2026, India’s contingent is made up of one archer, one athlete, two badminton players, two boxers, one equestrian, one judoka, one sailor, two swimmers, one TT player, four (beach) wrestlers and one wushu fighter. The difference between the YOG and OG is that the athlete quota for a non-host country at the YOG depends on the international federation’s rules about the quotas. Athletics has only two — one male, one female — per non-host country, swimming has four — two male, two female, etc.But here is where it gets odd: there is no concise document freely available outlining YOG quotas across sport for contending participants and coaches or for the general public. This quota document, I was informed, is only made available to each National Sports Federation (NSF). The IOA should ask Indian NSFs to put out detailed information about where and how their athletes attempted YOG quotas spots and how they fared.Given that India has ambitions around hosting big events, you would think that there should be tremendous energy across sport into sending as many competitors to the YOG as they can. Rather than demonstrating a paucity of faith in the next generation.For sure, India didn’t need to attempt Dakar2026 quotas in baseball or breaking or 3x3 basketball. But among the other YOG2026 competition sports, what about fencing, gymnastics, road cycling, taekwondo, triathlon? We sent 20 fencers to Aichi-Nagoya2026 – suddenly they have no successors?As Alice said when in Wonderland, “curiouser and curiouser.”

articles.summary: ISRO NVS-03 launch: 5 things to know about India’s new navigation satellite The Hindu
articles.content: India’s independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC (Navigation with Indian Constellation) was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday (October 30, 2026) as ISRO successfully launched its 2,250 kg navigation satellite NVS-03 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota. GSLV places next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit storyline 1 Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained The mission could help restore the functioning of India’s regional satellite navigation system NavIC; its development began following the 1999 Kargil War, when the U.S reportedly clamped down on GPS data access Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained storyline 1 The satellite successfully separated from the launch vehicle and was injected into its intended Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). The satellite is the third in ISRO's next-generation navigation satellite series, envisaged to ensure continuity of navigation services under the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS). This mission aims to revive and modernise NavIC. Here’s what to know about India’s new navigation satellite, NVS-03, with a mission life of 12 years. Restoring a weakened NavIC network NavIC requires at least 4 active satellites to provide positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services. Following clock failures on older satellites and failure of NVS-02 to reach its final orbit, the operational fleet shrank to just 3 satellites. Placing NVS-03 into orbit provided the fourth satellite needed to restore standalone navigation services. Also read: NVS-03 launch highlights https://www.thehindu.com/sci-tech/science/isro-gslv-f18-nvs-03-navigation-satellite-launch-sriharikota-october-30-2026-live-updates/article71645088.ece Upgraded indegenous atomic clocks Atomic clocks are central to satellite navigation and helps calculate exact distances by measuring signal travel time. Older IRNSS satellites relied on imported Swiss clocks that repeatedly failed. NVS-03 carries a indigenously developed Rubidium atomic clock (developed by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre) alongside imported ones. This moves India closer to full self reliance in high precision space timing. Losing the way: On ISRO and issues with its NavIC constellation Losing the way: On ISRO and issues with its NavIC constellation ISRO must fix issues before launch of next second-generation satellites Losing the way: On ISRO and issues with its NavIC constellation editorial 1 L1 Brand integration for common smartphones NVS-03 transmits on the L1 frequency band in addition to the existing L5 and S bands. The L1 band is widely used in commercial GPS receivers, which will make it easier for everyday mobile chipsets to access Indian Standard Time and NavIC positioning signals. The system is designed to provide coverage over India’s landmass and an area extending 1,500 kilometres beyond its geopolitical boundary. Civilian and Defence applications NavIC offers two main services: an open signal for public navigation, mapping and logistics, and an encrypted restricted service for the military. The latter provides high-precision data essential for guiding missiles, tracking troop movements and operating defence platforms safely, practically acting as a strategic asset for India. Elaborating on NavIC’s civilian applications, the ISRO chief V. Narayanan said 10,400 locomotives and 64,000 fishing vessels are currently tracked in real time. Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana, the agency aims to expand this to 1 lakh fishing vessels within the next six months. In total, 15 lakh tracking devices have been fitted across vehicles. When asked when NavIC would be available on civilian mobile phones, Narayanan stated this would happen once the full seven-satellite constellation is completed. History India began developing NavIC after Global Positioning System (GPS) access was restricted by the U.S. during the 1999 Kargil War. The first-generation IRNSS satellites were launched between 2013 and 2018, with nine satellites launched during that period. The newly launched NVS-03 brings the total of the entire NavIC programme to 12 satellites. Operating an independent regional satellite system will ensure India’s positioning and timing capabilities remain secure during geopolitical conflicts. “India has got a navigation programme. And as per the programme, we are supposed to provide navigation services for India plus 1,500 kilometres from the Indian border, called the Regional Navigation Service. For that, seven satellites are supposed to be in orbit,” Mr. Narayanan said. He said NVS-03 was the fourth satellite launched under the programme and added that the entire constellation would have to be completed before the navigation service could be integrated with mobile systems for wider public use. Highlighting the significance of the indigenous atomic clock onboard the satellite, Mr. Narayanan said two such clocks were already functioning in orbit, and the third had now been placed in space. The GSLV-F18 was the 20th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle. (With inputs from agencies)

articles.title: GSLV places next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit - The Hindu
articles.summary: GSLV places next-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 into orbit The Hindu
articles.content: Bengaluru The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18) on Friday (October 30, 2026) successfully launched the NVS-03 satellite from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, according to the ISRO. The GSLV-F18 with the NVS-03 satellite lifted off from the second launch pad of the spaceport and, 18 minutes later placed the satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. “The GSLV-F18 vehicle has successfully and precisely injected the NVS-03 satellite weighing 2250 kg in the intended elliptical orbit. Let me congratulate each and every team member of ISRO, industrial partners, academia for this outstanding accomplishment,” ISRO Chairman Dr. V. Narayanan said. He added that the vehicle systems have performed as predicted and as expected. Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained The mission could help restore the functioning of India’s regional satellite navigation system NavIC; its development began following the 1999 Kargil War, when the U.S reportedly clamped down on GPS data access Why is ISRO’s NVS-03 satellite launch crucial? | Explained storyline 1 The 2250 kg NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next-generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) series or the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC). According to the ISRO, the satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock, along with procured atomic clocks. “It also includes L1 signal in addition to existing L5/S signals with coverage over India landmass and a region extending 1,500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary,” the ISRO said. With NavIC setback, India unable to use satellite system for security purposes: experts With NavIC setback, India unable to use satellite system for security purposes: experts A major setback occurred after the last atomic clock on board the Indian Regional Navigational Satellite System-1F (IRNSS-1F) stopped functioning on March 10, leaving only three satellites of the NavIC constellation in function; armed forces of countries use the navigation satellite system for logistics, mapping and operational planning, and relying on a foreign navigation satellite system could pose security issues, especially during wars With NavIC setback, India unable to use satellite system for security purposes: experts storyline 1 NavIC is India’s independent regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate position, navigation, and Timing (PNT) services to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area. The successful launch of the NVS-03, which will have a mission life of 12 years, is expected to restore the functioning of the NavIC constellation, which has been weakened due to repeated failures of atomic clocks and the ISRO’s inability to place its previous replacement satellite, NVS-02, in its intended orbit. It can be recalled that earlier this year, on March 13, the last functioning atomic clock aboard IRNSS-1F had stopped working. The ISRO Chairman said that with the success of the mission, the NavIC constellation is restored to the minimum operational configuration with four satellites. “Already three satellites are successfully working in orbit, with this satellite we will have four satellites and restore the PNT services of the country. As you know, the NavIC constellation is a strategic national asset that provides the nation independent access to PNT services. It is also used for civilian applications like real-time tracking of trains along with tracking of vehicles and shipping vessels. It is an important component of the One Nation One Time Project,” the ISRO Chairman said. Friday’s (October 30, 2026) launch is only the third mission to be launched by ISRO in 2026, after the PSLV-C62 mission carrying the EOS-N1 Earth observation satellite on January 12, 2026, and the EOS-05 aboard the GSLV-F17 on September 4. While the PSLV-C62 mission was a failure, the GSLV-F17 mission was a success. “This mission was accomplished with the least turnaround time of just 56 days between successive GSLV missions,” Dr. Narayanan said. PM Modi congratulates ISRO Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated ISRO for the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03. “This mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, our indigenous satellite navigation system,” Mr. Modi said in a post on X. The dedication and ingenuity of our space scientists continue to make our nation proud, he added.

articles.title: Maharashtra suspends four FDA officials over hookah tobacco lapses - India Today
articles.summary: Maharashtra suspends four FDA officials over hookah tobacco lapses India Today
articles.content: The Maharashtra government has suspended four Food and Drug Administration officials, including two assistant commissioners, over alleged procedural lapses while taking action against manufacturers and traders of flavoured and scented hookah tobacco products, news agency Press Trust of India reported.Departmental inquiries have also been ordered against the four officials of the Food and Drug Administration, the state's food safety regulator. The suspension orders were issued on Friday by the Medical Education and Drugs Department, under which the regulator functions.The officials are D V Bhogawade, Assistant Commissioner (Food), Pune; Y B Dahatonde, Assistant Commissioner (Food), Nagpur; and food safety officers C R Swami and A Y Ilager. They were posted in Pune, Nagpur and Solapur.The action follows proceedings against Ms SOEX India Pvt Ltd and Ms High Street Impex LLP over flavoured and scented hookah tobacco products. The products carried declarations stating that they were not meant for consumption and were intended only for smoking through hookahs.According to Press Trust of India, the suspension orders cited several common procedural shortcomings in the handling of the cases.
